title: functioncall-emergent-regression-simulator-2026
author: Sasha Kim
body:
Overview

This document describes the Functioncall Emergent Regression Simulator (FERS) — a reproducible harness and failure-library designed to synthesize and stress emergent failure modes for function-calling models during shadow, canary, and quantized rollouts. FERS is intended to detect behavioral regressions that do not appear in standard prompt suites: e.g., degraded function argument extraction, hallucinated tool endpoints, corrupted JSON shapes, and latent tokenization-induced misalignment under quantization.

Goals

- Provide a catalog of synthetic failure generators targeting functioncall interfaces.
- Define a runtime harness (eval-meson) that can inject failures into shadow traffic and produce deterministic failure traces.
- Supply acceptance criteria and automated triage signals to gate rollouts (shadow -> canary -> prod) for models with functioncall usage.
- Standardize remediation and rollforward steps for regressions discovered by the simulator.

Scope and applicability

- Applies to models exposed via Redwood API's chat/functioncall surface and internal rerankers that emit structured payloads.
- Intended for model onboarding, quant migration, and canary validations across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
- Not intended as a replacement for human annotator evaluations; FERS augments evaluator workflows by surfacing falsifiable, reproducible failure traces.

Definitions

- Failure generator: deterministic or stochastic transformer that mutates prompts, responses, or function signatures to simulate a class of regression.
- Anchor probe: a canonical prompt-and-response pair used for day-zero comparison and SLI calculation.
- Emergent regression: behavior change that appears only under composite conditions (e.g., long context + quant + functioncall).

Failure-library (catalog)

Below is an excerpt of the curated failure generators. The full library is in repo: git://infra/eval-meson/fers/failure-library.

| id | target | description | intensity knobs | expected signal |
|----|--------|-------------|-----------------|----------------|
| FCF-01 | function-args | Drop a random required arg from the model-invoked JSON payload | drop_rate (0.0-1.0) | increase in missing-arg errors; schema-violation count up |
| FCF-02 | json-escape | Inject mis-escaped control characters into string args | char_freq, char_set | parser exceptions or silent truncation |
| FCF-03 | endpoint-halluc | Replace real tool names with plausible-but-invalid endpoints | substitution_map_size | 4xx/5xx tool routing anomalies; increased fallback triggers |
| FCF-04 | token-shift | Shift token boundaries to simulate tokenization drift (quant-sensitive) | shift_window, seed | coherence drop on long-context slices; KV-cache misses |
| FCF-05 | type-corrupt | Replace numeric args with strings and vice-versa | corruption_rate | type-mismatch traces in downstream services |

Design and architecture

High-level components: eval-meson (harness), probeforge (probe generator), sidecar-evaluator (per-tenant evaluator-sidecar), and synth-catalog (failure library).

- eval-meson: Gateway that replays or mirrors shadow traffic and coordinates injection via a pluggable failure step graph. Supports deterministic seeds for reproducible traces.
- probeforge: DSL for composing multi-step probes (priming -> invoke -> verify). Probe definitions are stored as YAML manifests and can target live shadow traffic, synthetic sessions, or archived traces.
- sidecar-evaluator: Runs near the serving tier (dedicated/private) and evaluates functioncall stability at socket-level to catch protocol anomalies before they hit upstream tooling.
- synth-catalog: Versioned package of failure generators with semantic versioning. Each generator includes a risk score and recommended mitigation patterns.

Operational flow (high level)

1) Author creates a probe manifest in probeforge (see example below).
2) eval-meson schedules the probe against a shadow cohort or synthetic session set.
3) Failure generators run according to configured intensity; traces are recorded to S3 and the eval-meson results store.
4) Automated analyzers compute SLI deltas vs. anchors and emit triage tickets if thresholds are breached.
5) Triage flow routes to the model-oncall and quant-steering desk with recommended rollback/mitigation actions.

Probe manifest example (YAML)

---
name: invoice-extraction-longcontext
mode: shadow
seed: 20260610-invoice-001
steps:
  - priming: file://probes/primers/invoice-context-12k.txt
  - call: { model: gpt-4x-functioncall-v0, max_tokens: 256, function: extract_invoice }
  - failure_inject:
      id: FCF-04
      params: { shift_window: 128, seed: 42 }
  - verify: { schema: file://schemas/invoice-v2.json, allow_missing_fields: false }

Running the simulator (CLI examples)

# Run a single probe against archived trace set
$ eval-meson run --probe invoice-extraction-longcontext --archive s3://eval-archives/tenant-a/2026-06-01 --seed 42

# Schedule a multichoort run with increasing intensity
$ eval-meson schedule --manifest ./manifests/quant-compat-multi.yaml --cohorts tenant-a,tenant-b --ramp 0.1:0.5:1.0 --notify --deadline 2026-06-20

Acceptance criteria and gating rules

All rollouts that include functioncall-capable models must pass the following checks in the shadow stage before canary:

- Anchor coherence SLI: delta <= 1.5% against promoted baseline on the anchor probes after 1000 probe runs.
- Schema conformance: no more than 0.2% schema violations on critical fields (invoice_id, total_amount) across the shadow cohort.
- Tool stability: < 0.5% increase in tool fallback rate when endpoint-hallucation generators are enabled at intensity=0.25.
- Token-shift sensitivity: coherence p95 drop < 2% under FCF-04 intensity=0.5 for long-context probes.

If any single gating rule fails, the model must not proceed to canary and the model owner must open a regression investigation within 1 business day.

Monitoring, alerts and triage signals

Primary signals produced by FERS:

- SLI delta per-anchor (numerical): stored as time-series metric ers.anchor.delta_{probe_name}
- Schema violation rate (percentage) ers.schema.violation_{model}_{schema}
- Tool fallback increment ers.tool.fallback_delta_{model}
- Reproducibility score (0-1): fraction of injected failures that reproduce across seeds (low score indicates non-deterministic failure)

Alerting thresholds (examples):

- P0: schema violation rate >= 1% sustained for 5 minutes -> page oncall + create incident ticket.
- P1: anchor SLI delta >= 3% for 30 minutes -> notify model owner and schedule regression run.
- P2: reproducibility score < 0.3 on high-severity failure generators -> send to evaluation desk for manual analysis.

Automated triage rules

- If schema violation rate > 0.5% && reproducibility >= 0.75 -> auto-open a regression-investigation ticket with attached failure traces and suggested blame candidates (quant, tokenizer, prompt-preprocessor).
- If token-shift sensitivity triggers with low tool fallback changes -> flag quant as likely cause and pin a quant_shadow cohort for deeper replay.

Investigation and remediation checklist (numbered runbook)

1. Confirm reproducibility: re-run failing probe with seed and verify failure trace (eval-meson replay --trace <id>).
2. Compare traces across promoted baseline and candidate model; capture tokenization diffs.
3. If tokenization drift suspected, run token-shift diagnostic (probeforge diagnostics token-diff).
4. If quant-sensitive: route to quant-steering; run mixed-precision shadow with FCF-04 intensity sweep.
5. If function-arg or JSON corruption: run sidecar-evaluator at socket level and check intermediate tool ingress logs.
6. Apply mitigations: prompt-rewrite, schema-relaxation (short-term), or quant rollback (if severity high).
7. Re-run gated probes and ensure all acceptance criteria pass before resuming rollout.

Owner and escalation matrix

- Library owner: Sasha Kim (applied-evals).
- Harness owner: Marcus Liu (eval infra).
- Quant desk: Diego Ramirez (applied-ml).
- Oncall: model-oncall rotation (see team wiki for schedule).

Change controls and release cadence

- synth-catalog updates require a PR with: description of new generator, risk score, two reviewers, and reproducibility report (>= 10 deterministic seeds).
- Minor patch releases (catalog patch) on a two-week cadence. Major changes that affect gating thresholds require sign-off from quant desk and evaluation committee and a 1-week canary run across two tenants.

Appendix A — Example failure trace snippet (trimmed JSON)

{
  "probe_id": "invoice-extraction-longcontext",
  "seed": 42,
  "failure_gen": "FCF-04",
  "events": [
    {"t":"2026-06-10T12:01:02Z","stage":"call","tokens_before": 10234},
    {"t":"2026-06-10T12:01:03Z","stage":"inject","desc":"shifted tokens at 100-228"},
    {"t":"2026-06-10T12:01:04Z","stage":"verify","result":"schema_violation","field":"total_amount"}
  ]
}

Appendix B — Quickcheck list before submitting a promo PR

- [ ] Add anchor probe + baseline results to PR description.
- [ ] Include reproducibility score and failure traces for all enabled generators.
- [ ] Confirm no schema regressions on critical fields (invoice_id, user_id, total).
- [ ] Run token-shift diagnostic at intensity 0.5 and include report.
